title: Low-Sodium Silky Saudi-Arabian Duck-Confit-Leg Tagine
description: A cultured, silky, and cozy Saudi-Arabian dish featuring duck-confit-leg, perfect for a low-sodium diet. This hearty tagine is simmered in a clay vessel, releasing the rich flavors of the confit.
instructions: Preheat the clay tagine or a heavy Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add the ghee or neutral oil and brown the duck confit legs until crispy on all sides.
Remove the duck from the pot and set aside.
Add the chopped onion to the pot and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and grated ginger to the pot and cook for 1 minute.
Add the ras el hanout spice blend and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add the canned diced tomatoes, chicken broth, and honey to the pot.
Return the duck confit legs to the pot and bring to a simmer.
Cover the pot with a tight-fitting lid and transfer to the preheated oven.
Braise the tagine for 2 hours, or until the duck is tender and the sauce has thickened.
Garnish with chopped fresh cilantro and serve over couscous or rice.
